motivation: Original across-category analysis (helped vs hurt) has definitional confound: helped = pure-wrong (naturally high |loglik|), hurt = pure-right (naturally lower |loglik|). Within-category controls eliminate this confound by comparing only within pure-correct or only within pure-wrong.

margin_semantics.pure_correct: higher |loglik| = lower probability = less confident correct = closer to boundary
margin_semantics.pure_wrong: lower |loglik| = higher probability for target = near-miss = closer to boundary

method.control_1: Within pure-correct: hurt (pure-right, hybrid-wrong) vs stayed-right (pure-right, hybrid-right)
method.control_2: Within pure-wrong: helped (pure-wrong, hybrid-right) vs stayed-wrong (pure-wrong, hybrid-wrong)

hypotheses.C1: hurt has higher |loglik| than stayed-right (less confident correct → vulnerable)
hypotheses.C2: helped has lower |loglik| than stayed-wrong (near-miss wrong → rescuable)

method.note: GDN uses h12-1 (1.3B h3-1 unavailable); RetNet/HGRN2 use h3-1

control_1_pure_correct.interpretation: Hurt samples had higher abs(loglik) = lower target probability = less confident correct. Supports hypothesis: weakly-correct answers are vulnerable to attention flipping.

control_2_pure_wrong.interpretation: Helped samples had lower abs(loglik) = higher target probability = near-miss wrong. Supports hypothesis: near-miss wrong answers are rescuable by attention.

cross_arch_summary: Both controls significant across all 3 architectures with expected directions. C1: hurt samples were less confident correct (higher |loglik|) than stayed-right — weakly-correct answers are vulnerable to attention flipping. C2: helped samples were near-miss wrong (lower |loglik|) vs stayed-wrong — near-miss wrong answers are rescuable by attention. Confidence margin genuinely predicts per-example attention effect, NOT a definitional artifact of the across-category comparison.
